prompt: A language learner chooses practice dialogues she can already complete perfectly, every time, because success feels motivating. Her level stays flat for months. What is the problem?

options.text: She practises too regularly for progress to occur
Dialogues are not a valid way to learn a language at all
Practice set entirely inside current ability gives no new information; she needs material slightly beyond her level, where some errors occur and can be corrected
She should choose dialogues so hard she understands nothing

explanation: This is the desirable-difficulty balance: perfect success means the task is below her level, while total incomprehension gives nothing to build on. Slightly-too-hard, with feedback, is where learning happens.
